answer: A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, thus paying the horizon bond on all of them and exposing each to the crystal slash. Because the juniper audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 9 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. Each impostor pays 16 dollars up front. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
